hero.name: Akshay Ujjani Narasimhaiah
hero.role: Process & Project Engineer: process optimization, thermal processes and CFD
hero.bio: I'm a process engineer based in Magdeburg. For two years I ran tunnel kilns, drying plants and steam generators at a roof-tile plant. After that I spent two years at Otto-von-Guericke University Magdeburg researching how process control affects the energy demand of microwave dryers. I also build simulation models in OpenFOAM and COMSOL to answer practical plant questions about energy use, safety and throughput. I'm looking for a role in Germany in process engineering, plant engineering, project engineering or simulation.

projects.title: Microwave drying of roof tiles (research project, OVGU)
projects.problem: Gas-fired convective dryers use a lot of energy. Microwave drying could cut energy use by 50% and lead time by 75%, but how the process is run decides how much of that is achieved.
projects.whatIDid: In a BMWK-funded IGF research project, I designed and ran the test plan for roof tiles and characterised the microwave dryer with impedance tuning, reflected-power measurements and energy balances. I formulated the drying model, built 3D electromagnetic and thermal simulations of the whole drying chamber in COMSOL Multiphysics, and coordinated the technical upgrade of the laboratory dryer with the project partner MFPA Weimar.
projects.result: Project report, results presented at one national and two international conferences, and one publication.

publication.text: Abstract in the Book of Abstracts of the 2nd International Workshop on Particle-Gas Systems (CRC 2025)

projects.title: Anode water separator for PEM electrolysis (master thesis, FEST GmbH)
projects.problem: Modular PEM electrolyzer systems need a separator vessel that reliably separates the oxygen from the water leaving the anode, in a vessel that is as compact as possible.
projects.whatIDid: I implemented a CFD model of the two-phase separation in the anode water separator and compared baffle-plate designs and operating pressures.
projects.result: I found the best baffle-plate design and operating pressure, and showed how much separation efficiency depends on the vessel length. FEST used the results to optimize and scale up the separator.

images.alt: Computational mesh of the horizontal separator vessel with its inlet and outlet nozzles
Simulated oxygen streamlines inside the separator vessel

projects.title: Explosion-protection zone for a hydrogen vent line (internship, FEST GmbH)
projects.problem: The Ex-zone around the vent line of a PEM electrolysis plant had been estimated too large.
projects.whatIDid: I simulated the hydrogen release from the vent line for several wind cases with FDS and Fluent and evaluated the results in Smokeview.
projects.result: A simulation-based Ex-zone that replaced the previously overestimated zone.

images.alt: FDS simulation of the hydrogen plume rising from the vent line
Simulation domain with the vent, meshed finer around the release

projects.title: Cycle-time reduction for feed pump sliding tappets (Bosch Limited)
projects.problem: Finishing the sliding tappets for feed pumps took two machining steps and limited the output per shift.
projects.whatIDid: In a four-person student project at Bosch, we optimized the grinding parameters with the Taguchi method so that one grinding step replaced grinding plus super-finishing.
projects.result: Shorter cycle time and higher output per shift, with one machining step and its machine no longer needed.
